objective: Formalize a controller-led multi-pass Rhino modeling architecture: ChatGPT Web authors each modeling pass, the local operator executes and returns evidence, and the controller uses that evidence to author the next targeted refinement pass. Keep the orientation concise and put the detailed state machine in workflow/payload documentation.
instructions: Read Phase 17 and Phase 18 evidence and preserve the proven controller-authored payload workflow.
This phase is control-plane/documentation/template work only. Do not modify Rhino/MCP runtime implementation and do not execute geometry-changing Rhino code.

Architecture principle: complex modeling should normally be iterative rather than one-shot. Each modeling pass is controller-authored, hash-verified, executed locally, validated/captured, returned through Git, reviewed by the controller, then followed by a new controller-authored pass if needed.

Do not make Claude the visual/modeling decision-maker. Claude may inspect, measure, validate, capture, save, and report objective evidence. Claude must not decide how to redesign geometry or author the next refinement payload.
Codex follows the same default. Codex may author or repair modeling code locally only when the active request explicitly grants local_modeling_authorized=true.

Use a separate structured bridge task/request for each consequential modeling pass so the controller receives evidence between passes. Do not hide multiple autonomous redesign passes inside one local operator task.
Define a stable modeling_run_id that links all passes belonging to one model/build while each pass retains its own task_id, branch, payload hash, report, and result commit.

Define the recommended three-pass default for complex reference-driven modeling without making it mandatory: Pass 1 FOUNDATION = primary proportions, topology/solid strategy, major dimensions/features; Pass 2 CORRECTION = controller compares returned measurements/captures/references and targets a bounded set of highest-impact discrepancies; Pass 3 DETAIL_QA = final detail, cleanup, dimensional/geometry QA, and artifact finalization. Allow extra or skipped passes when the task warrants it.

The controller, not the local operator, selects the correction targets for the next pass. A useful default for Pass 2 is a bounded top-N discrepancy list such as 3-5 high-impact issues, but do not hardcode five as a protocol requirement.

Add .bridge/workflows/MULTI_PASS_RHINO.md as the canonical detailed workflow guide. Include lifecycle, role boundaries, pass taxonomy, evidence loop, failure/retry behavior, stop conditions, and an example three-pass sequence.
Update .bridge/payloads/README.md to reference the multi-pass workflow and explain how payloads relate across passes.

Extend .bridge/templates/rhino-payload-manifest-v1.json backward-compatibly with optional multi-pass metadata: modeling_run_id, pass_index, pass_kind, parent_task_id, parent_payload_sha256, parent_result_commit, and requires_controller_review_after. Existing manifests without these fields must remain valid.

Create .bridge/templates/rhino-pass-evaluation-v1.json defining a consistent operator evidence packet for each pass. Include task_id, modeling_run_id, pass_index, executed_payload_sha256, document identity, object/result summary, measurements, validation summary, capture artifacts, save artifact, objective discrepancies/observations, retries/errors, and operator_recommendation_scope='evidence_only'.

Add a concise multi-pass principle to AI_ORIENTATION.md: complex modeling is normally controller-led and iterative; local operators return evidence between passes rather than autonomously redesigning.

Update controller.md with the controller loop: author payload -> execute -> inspect returned evidence/captures -> choose bounded correction targets -> author next payload -> repeat until acceptance criteria are met.
Update operator.md with the operator loop: execute exact payload -> collect standardized evidence -> stop and hand back to controller. No autonomous next-pass geometry authoring.
Update reviewer.md to verify pass lineage: modeling_run_id, parent task/payload/result references, executed SHA, and absence of unauthorized local modeling.

Update .bridge/protocol.json with a backward-compatible multi_pass_modeling section documenting controller-led pass semantics. Keep protocol_version 0.3 unless a schema-breaking change is genuinely required.
Optionally add lightweight fields to the example payload manifest demonstrating pass_index=1/pass_kind=foundation only if this does not complicate the safe fixture.
Do not make run_rhino_payload.py depend on the optional multi-pass fields. It should continue to execute both old and new manifests unchanged.

Add .bridge/evidence/bridge-phase19-001/multi-pass-architecture.json documenting the architecture, file map, pass state transitions, default three-pass strategy, role boundaries, backward compatibility, and validation results.

Validate all edited JSON with Python json.load, dry-run the existing _example payload to prove compatibility, run python3 -m py_compile .bridge/run_rhino_payload.py, run git diff --check, and verify protected Rhino/MCP runtime files are unchanged.
Commit implementation/evidence as the work commit and capture RESULT_COMMIT.
Create .bridge/reports/bridge-phase19-001.json with ack exactly BRIDGE-PHASE19-MULTIPASS-20260924-51AF3C-OPERATOR-ACK, exact base_commit, RESULT_COMMIT, and branch operator/bridge-phase19-001.
Run python3 .bridge/bridge_cli.py verify-report bridge-phase19-001 and require REPORT_OK.
Commit the report separately, push operator/bridge-phase19-001, and do not merge it.
constraints: ChatGPT Web remains the default author of every modeling/refinement payload.
Claude returns evidence and never autonomously redesigns geometry.
Codex local modeling still requires explicit request authorization.
Existing single-pass payloads and run_rhino_payload.py behavior must remain compatible.
No dependency installation, force push, or merge.
